pass: A pass is one loop review of the queue that records the actions chosen for its items.
wait: A wait is a derived statement that nothing is added after an ending yet, naming its reason and the mover that can still act.
action: An action is the next operation the loop chose for an item, such as dispatch, judge, settle, or wait.
lane: Lane is retired: an item acquires a worktree and scratch, scheduled against the running-agent limit.
node: A node is one act in an item's graph (an agent invocation, a command, a landing, or an owner question) and holds its own execution data.
path: A path is the started nodes of an item's graph, in order: the whole of what happened to the item.
run: A run is one node's execution record: its process segments, log, lease, declared outputs, ending and spend.
candidate: A candidate is a committed result from a run that can be checked for landing.
gate: A gate is the set of checks that judges whether a candidate is safe to land.
landing: A landing is the recorded application of an accepted candidate to the repository's shared branch.
heartbeat: A heartbeat is the loop's periodically refreshed record showing that its process is still alive.
session: A session is one harness conversation: the transcript a model continues from across nodes.
loop: A loop is one long-running process of the drain, recorded from its start through its last heartbeat and stop.
